content.title: UConn Coach Dann Hurley’s Wife Andrea Sirakides Has “Zero Interest” in College Basketball
content.text: 4 min readUConn Dan Hurley may be one of the top college basketball coaches in the country, but his wife Andrea is uninterested in the sport. She has “zero interest in the game,” she told the Post in 2021. “It’s like asking my husband to learn to knit. It’s just not going to happen.”As Hurley and the Huskies look to win another National Championship this evennig, however, Andrea will be cheering them on. “The players are honestly my favorite part. They’re other people’s kids, and they are away from home, so they need to know that someone is there for them,” she said. Every Mother’s Day, she revealed, she hears from past players. “I’m literally crying all day because it’s so insane that these kids think to text you.”In another interview, she said, “Every single team that you have, every kid that comes into your life. I always say it just snags a little piece of my heart. His heart. I love these kids and the coaches and the coaches’ families so much that I don’t want this to end. Like you’re not going to get this time back.”Eugene Gologursky//Getty ImagesThe Hurleys in November 2025.Advertisement - Continue Reading BelowHere’s what to know about Dan Hurley’s wife, Andrea Hurley (née Sirakides):Andrea and Dan met as students at Seaton Hall.As Dan told WTNH in March 2023, “It’s like, by far, the best thing that happened to me at Seton Hall, but that was the thing that saved my life when I met her and changed my life and made me want to be better.”They married in 1997, and have two sons: Danny (b. 1999) and Danny (b. 2002). “I don’t have a lot of friends, to be honest. Andrea and my boys are who I have, and they’re my world,” Dan told FOX Sports in January 2023. At home, Andrea joked to WTNH, “I’m in charge. I’m 1,000% in charge, and they’re all afraid of me, including the big guy.”“We got married when I was 20,” Andrea said this weekend. “I think there is a higher power that put us together. We are the best team. I can handle him, I humble him, I cheer him on, we’re a good team. I don’t know if there is anyone else in the world that could handle him, so God picked me.”She hosted a “Ball is Wife” podcast.Andrea cohosted the podcast, which aired in 2021 and 2022, with Nicole Kellogg, wife of Derek Kellogg. Ball is Wife was about “what life is like when sports are your in-laws.”“Who else feels like us,” she told the Athletic. “Is anybody else going through this? What do other coaches’ wives do on game day? What do other coaches’ wives do when you have four losses in a row? Like, what do you do? How do you feel? What about your kids? How are your kids reacting to this profession and the good and the bad that come with it? So after a while, I’m like every time we meet up, we say the same thing. I’m like, you know, it’s time. Somebody has to do it. Just so other people could relate.”She added, “When you start from the beginning, you understand what it takes to get to this point. You are going to make more sacrifices than you ever thought — your children are, you are. Let me tell you something, you have to be a tough broad to be a college coach’s wife.”Andrea makes Dan’s lunch every day.“When you figure out how you could help your other half get better at what he does, and you see it come back to you,” Andrea told WTNH. “It’s a friendship. It’s working together as a team. I try to make his life easier in any way that I possibly can.”She added that a lot of that comes from the little things, like “making his lunch every day. It’s it really is. It’s like making dinner every night and making sure that you, you know, still connect as a family.” For lunch, “Every day, it’s a salad. I wash blueberries and raspberries every single morning. And then it’s the same salad. We just change up the dressing every single morning. Anything he likes. I try to fill his world up with.”She fundraises for cancer treatment with Coaches vs. Cancer.Her dad, Ken Sirakides, died of colon cancer in 2005. Since, she’s been working to raise money for cancer treatment. “I don’t want anybody to ever feel like I felt with my dad,” she said in 2016. “He’s missed so much.”She added, “I know we’ve come so far with treatment. Go get your physical. Yearly physicals are so important — they can detect cancer early. If you can detect it early enough, then your survival rate is so much better with the treatment we have today.”Emily Burack (she/her) is the Deputy Digital Editor for Town & Country, where she covers entertainment, celebrities, the royals, and a wide range of other topics. Before joining T&C, she was the deputy managing editor at Hey Alma, a Jewish culture site. Follow her @emburack on Instagram, Twitter, and other social media platforms.
